name: Code2Prompt
relevance: Builds repository context and token-counted prompts for coding agents
notes: Uses the macOS/Linux Homebrew CLI formula. Select repositories, filters and output options explicitly. Skills and MCP configuration are separate steps; generated context can contain source code and should be reviewed before sharing.

name: grepai
relevance: Searches code semantically and traces callers for coding-agent context
notes: Uses the upstream Homebrew tap with x64/arm64 macOS/Linux binaries. Requires an embedding provider such as local Ollama/LM Studio or a configured hosted provider. Initialize and index chosen repositories explicitly; model downloads, indexing, watch mode and MCP setup are separate steps.

name: llmfit
relevance: Matches local language models and inference runtimes to available agent hardware
notes: Uses the macOS/Linux Homebrew formula. Hardware fit estimates depend on the selected model/backend. Install model runtimes and explicitly download, benchmark or serve models separately; installation does not start inference or submit benchmark results.

name: Fabric AI
relevance: Runs reusable language-model patterns and pipelines for agent-assisted workflows
notes: Uses the macOS/Linux fabric-ai Homebrew formula, whose executable is fabric-ai rather than fabric. It is distinct from the unrelated Python Fabric SSH tool. Run setup and select providers, patterns and inputs explicitly; pattern refreshes and model requests are separate steps.

name: Browserbase Browse
relevance: Gives agents browser control, web telemetry and Browserbase platform commands
notes: Requires Node 20.19+ on the 20.x line or Node 22.12+. The official CLI is npm browse from browserbase/stagehand, not the Stagehand SDK or legacy bb CLI. Configure local Chrome/Chromium or Browserbase credentials separately. Browser commands can start a daemon/session; cloud calls can consume credits. Installation does not start a browser.

name: OpenAgents Control
relevance: Installs and manages coding-agent patterns, context and OpenCode workflows
notes: The npm package declares Node 14+, while current upstream development uses Node 18+; use a current Node runtime. Requires Bash 3.2+, Git and OpenCode for agent workflows; Windows needs Git Bash or WSL. Installing the wrapper does not install agent patterns or configure a project; run OAC setup/install explicitly.

name: Cisco MCP Scanner
relevance: Analyzes MCP tool definitions and server code with configurable security scanners
notes: Requires Python 3.11.4+; upstream selects Python 3.13. Set UV_PYTHON=3.13 when installing to select that interpreter. YARA and other native dependencies may need platform build tools. Choose scan targets/engines explicitly; live-server scans can execute server commands or contact services. Hosted/LLM analysis and VirusTotal need separate credentials.

name: MCP Filesystem Server
relevance: Provides configured local filesystem tools to agent MCP clients
notes: Uses the official @modelcontextprotocol/server-filesystem package and mcp-server-filesystem executable. Use a current Node runtime for SDK dependencies. Configure MCP clients and explicitly choose allowed directories before starting the server; filesystem access is limited by that configuration. Installation does not register or start an MCP server.

name: Pydantic AI CLI
relevance: Runs Pydantic AI agents and terminal conversations through the clai client
notes: Requires Python 3.11+. Installs the official clai distribution, which includes the pydantic-ai dependency, rather than relying on the pai compatibility alias. This catalog method targets macOS/Linux terminal platforms. Configure model providers and choose custom agents or tools explicitly.

name: Hayhooks
relevance: Deploys Haystack agent and retrieval pipelines as HTTP and MCP endpoints
notes: Requires Python 3.10 through 3.14. The hayhooks distribution supplies its CLI. Define pipeline wrappers and install pipeline-specific dependencies in the chosen environment separately. Deployment, server startup, MCP exposure and provider credentials are explicit setup steps.

name: MLX LM
relevance: Runs local language models and OpenAI-compatible inference for Apple silicon agents
notes: Requires Python 3.11+ and Apple silicon macOS 14+ with a compatible MLX/Metal backend. This entry uses the base macOS distribution; Linux CPU/CUDA extras are not installed. Select models and explicitly download, chat, fine-tune or start mlx_lm.server separately; memory requirements depend on the model.

name: Arize Phoenix CLI
relevance: Serves tracing, inspection and evaluation tools for agent applications
notes: Requires Python 3.11 through 3.14. The arize-phoenix package supplies phoenix and arize-phoenix. Start the local service explicitly; configure storage, tracing exporters, instrumentation, authentication and evaluation providers separately. Application instrumentation can send trace content to the configured endpoint.

name: Langflow CLI
relevance: Builds, runs and serves visual agent workflows and MCP-enabled flows
notes: Requires Python 3.10 through 3.14. Langflow is a metapackage; expose the langflow-base dependency executable with uv --with-executables-from langflow-base while retaining langflow for inventory, upgrades and removal. Older AgentManager binaries must be upgraded/rebuilt for this metadata support. Start the service and configure flow dependencies, providers, storage and authentication explicitly.

name: Apify CLI
relevance: Develops and runs web-extraction Actors that provide data and tools to agents
notes: The published CLI requires Node 20+; current upstream development targets Node 22+. Uses apify-cli rather than an Apify SDK; it also installs actor and apify-cli aliases. Create projects and authenticate explicitly. Local runs need their project/browser dependencies; cloud Actor runs or deployments can consume account resources.

name: Magentic UI CLI
relevance: Launches a human-supervised computer-use agent interface and backend
notes: Requires Python 3.12+. The current upstream MagenticLite release tests macOS arm64 and Windows x64 through WSL2; native Linux x64 is expected but untested upstream. This catalog method supports macOS/Linux, with Windows users running inside WSL. Quicksand VM setup, Linux KVM access, model credentials and service startup are separate requirements.

name: Marvin CLI
relevance: Extracts and transforms structured data through agentic language-model workflows
notes: Requires Python 3.10+. The marvin package supplies the CLI, including stdin extraction via marvin x and configuration/database commands. Configure model providers and storage explicitly. Model-backed operations can send selected input to the configured provider; installation does not execute a workflow.

name: llama-swap
relevance: Routes agent model requests and swaps local inference-server processes
notes: Uses the upstream Homebrew tap with x64/arm64 macOS/Linux binaries. Install inference backends, choose models and prepare a configuration separately. Starting the proxy can launch configured model-server commands; installation does not start it or download models.

name: BentoML CLI
relevance: Packages and serves model inference APIs used by agent applications
notes: Requires Python 3.9+. The bentoml distribution supplies its CLI; model/framework dependencies belong in the selected service environment. Define services and configure models explicitly. Container builds need Docker, and cloud deployment needs separate account/authentication setup; installation does not deploy a service.

name: Chroma CLI
relevance: Runs and manages vector retrieval storage for agent memory and RAG workflows
notes: Requires Python 3.9+. The chromadb distribution supplies chroma. Published native wheels cover macOS x64 10.12+/arm64 11+, glibc 2.17+ Linux x64/arm64 and Windows x64; dependency requirements can be stricter. Choose storage and explicitly start a server or connect to cloud resources. Collection creation, embedding downloads and data ingestion are separate steps.

name: n8n CLI
relevance: Runs automation workflows that integrate agents, model calls and external tools
notes: Requires Node 24+. The npm n8n package includes the self-hosted workflow CLI/server, not a desktop app. Configure storage, encryption/authentication, credentials and workflow activation separately. Starting or executing workflows can call external services; installation does not start the service or activate workflows.
